* Flash Flood Warning for...
Clayton County in northeastern Iowa...
Fayette County in northeastern Iowa...

heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 3 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
West Union, Guttenberg, Elkader, Postville, Monona, Fayette,
McGregor, Garnavillo, Elgin, Clermont, Maynard, Hawkeye, Arlington,
Marquette, Farmersburg, Waucoma, Volga, Luana and Wadena.

dangers of flooding.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued September 19 at 4:03AM CDT by NWS Memphis TN
properties.description:
AQAMEG

The Shelby County Health Department has issued a Code Orange Ozone
Forecast effective for Shelby County Tennessee, Crittenden County
Arkansas, and DeSoto County Mississippi, including the city of
Memphis for today. This ozone forecast is due to forecasted ozone
values that will be unhealthy for sensitive groups. These values will
exceed the Environmental Protection Agency's federal safe health
standard. The Shelby County Health Department recommends that
sensitive groups which include active children and adults, and
people with respiratory disease, such as asthma, limit prolonged
outdoor exertion.

Please continue to check the latest air quality forecasts and updates
until monitored values return to safe levels. For more information go

properties.description:

evening and last through the weekend as multiple strong low pressure
systems move into the northern gulf. These lows will bring multiple
days of moderate to heavy rain, with around 1.5 to 3 inches of rain
every 24 hours. Some areas, especially near Yakutat and along the
gulf coast, could see localized areas reach around 4 inches of rain
in 24 hours. Heaviest rain rates are anticipated late Saturday into
Sunday with hourly rates of 0.15 to 0.3 inches possible. This heavy
rain will likely cause rapid river rises along smaller rivers and
streams, but no flooding is expected at this time for areas outside
the flood watch.

the area. Strongest winds are anticipated to occur late Saturday
into Sunday with 30 to 40 kts, gusts to 50 kts across the gulf and
20 to 35 kts, gusts around 40 to 50 kts across the northern inner
channels. Land winds will also increase, with areas especially along
the central gulf coast seeing wind gusts up to around 45 mph. Check
back for more updates through the weekend.

properties.areaDesc: Interior Kuskokwim Delta
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 18 at 4:14PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
ESFAFC

High water in the Kuskokwim River region will continue over the next
few days. Conditions are expected to become favorable for water
levels to gradually recede over the weekend and into the middle of
next week.

Locations:

* Communities across the lower Kuskokwim River and its tributaries,
including, but not limited to: Kwethluk, Bethel, Oscarville,
Napaskiak, Napkiak, Kasigluk, Nunapitchuk, and Atmauluak.

Hydrologic Concerns:

* High water in the Kuskokwim and other area rivers (e.g. Kwethluk
River, Johnson River, etc) may inundate low-lying areas in the
aforementioned communities, nearby fish camps, and other lowlands.

Details/Analysis [What's causing this?]:

* Rainfall: The Kuskokwim River basin, from the mouth at Kuskokwim
Bay upstream to the headwaters in the Alaska Range and Kilbuck
Mountains, has received approximately 150 to 200 percent of normal
rainfall this summer (June to August). These rains have continued
into September, with nearly the entire basin near or exceeding 200
percent of rainfall, with much of that rainfall occurring over the
last few days.

* Persistent High Water: This heavy rainfall has resulted in
anomalously high water levels being routed down from the Upper
Kuskokwim to the Lower Kuskokwim. The river gages at McGrath and
Crooked Creek are near or exceeding record levels for this time of
year. The water levels at these stations have crested in the last
week, suggesting that the water inflow to the lower Kuskokwim
Communities may be on the decrease soon.

* Compounding Factors: In addition to the recent rainfall and
elevated river levels, strong coastal winds brought several feet of
surge to the coast, causing elevated water levels near the mouth of
the Kuskokwim River. This effectively reduces the slope of the
river, slowing drainage and resulting in water becoming backed up.

* Forecast Thoughts: A shift in the weather pattern will bring
conditions favorable for water levels to decrease. Northerly winds
will increase Saturday and continue into early next week to 20 to
30 kt, with higher gusts possible at times, and bring cooler and
drier air to the region. Precipitation will be sparse and generally
light. Additionally, tidal models indicate a slight negative surge
along the coast due to the multi-day period of strong northerly
winds, potentially assisting drainage of water from the lower
Kuskokwim River.

Look Ahead:

* After a period of weather conditions favorable for receding water,
confidence is growing that another strong Bering Sea storm will
affect western Alaska late next week (Sept 23-26). A return to
southerly winds and higher coastal water in conjunction to heavy
rainfall may exacerbate river conditions once again, particularly
on the smaller tributaries such as the Kwethluk and Johnson Rivers.
However, details remain uncertain at this time as confidence is low
in storm track and intensity. Fortunately, natural tidal cycles in
Bethel and the rest of the lower Kuskokwim favor lower tides than
usual for this timeframe which may offset any additional water or
surge.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 18 at 2:52PM AKDT until September 21 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A series of low pressures will move through the panhandle this
weekend bringing prolonged rain combined with high freezing levels to
increase ice melt on glacier river systems. The heavy rainfall and
associated runoff will produce significant river rises with the
potential of minor flooding.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Including the following area, Northern Inner Channels. This
includes the cities of Skagway, White Pass, And Haines.

* WHEN...From late Saturday night through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A series of lows will bring a prolonged period of rain combined
with warmer temperatures aloft allowing for any precipitation
falling into the region to remain as rain. Current thinking is
that the rain will continue this evening into Saturday before a
second, stronger system moves in for Saturday into Sunday.
Between the two systems, the flow is expected to remain onshore
keeping moisture moving into the area.

For the Skagway area, 24 hour precip looks to get up to 1 to 2
inches this weekend while the storm total amounts could be 2 to 4
inches. The Haines area is expected to see 0.75 to 1.5 inches in
24 hours while a storm total precipitation of 2 to 3.5 inches is
possible.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Persons living along streams should stay alert and be prepared to
take action if a warning or advisory is issued, or flooding is
observed.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.description:
ESFRIW

A wet weather system will support periods of showers and
thunderstorms across Wyoming Friday, Saturday, and Sunday. This
weather system is funneling abundant tropical moisture into the
state. Given this anomalously high moisture, many thunderstorms will
feature heavy rainfall, possibly leading to localized flooding. Poor
drainage areas, urban areas, and steep terrain will be the most
susceptible locations for this isolated flooding.

Many locations could see rainfall totals anywhere between 0.75" to
1.75" through Sunday afternoon, with a majority of this rain falling
quickly in thunderstorms.

Remember, if you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around don't down!
